process.section_title: How it works - from brief to build to launch
process.section_subtitle: No surprises and no "we'll get back to you" that never does. Here is exactly what happens once you get in touch

steps.title: Scoping call
steps.description: We work out what your business does, what's stuck, and what the goal is. If we're not the right fit, we'll say so on this call.

steps.title: Proposal and scope
steps.description: One document: what we'll build, what we won't, what it costs and when it goes live. A final price, with nothing added along the way.

steps.title: Development in stages
steps.description: You see a live version in the first week and review as we go. No waiting in the dark until the end.

steps.title: Launch and support
steps.description: We deploy, test and stay with you. The first month of fixes and adjustments is included in the price.

faq.section_title: What a business website costs and how long it takes

items.question: What does a website cost?
items.answer: A business site usually starts in the low thousands, and a complex system with automations and integrations costs more. You'll get an exact range on the scoping call - not before we understand what you need, because any number before that is a guess.

items.question: How long does it take?
items.answer: A business site: 2-3 weeks. A system with automations: 4-6 weeks. The date is set in the proposal and we hold ourselves to it. If something slips on our side, you hear about it immediately, not at the end.

items.question: Who owns the code and the domain?
items.answer: You do. The domain is registered in your name, the code is handed over, and you are not locked in with us. If you want to continue with another developer you can, and that's completely fine.

items.question: What happens after launch?
items.answer: The first month of fixes and adjustments is included. After that you can work with us on a monthly maintenance plan or on demand - no commitment required.

items.question: Do you work with very small businesses?
items.answer: Yes. Some of our best projects have been one-person businesses drowning in manual work. If the budget doesn't stretch to a full project, we'll tell you what is worth doing with what you have.

items.question: What if we're not happy?
items.answer: We stay with it until it works. Working in stages is exactly why - you see output as we go, rather than discovering at the end that we went the wrong way.

about.section_title: Building websites for small businesses in Israel
paragraphs: PROPEL was founded on one simple belief: small and mid-sized businesses deserve the same standard of digital execution large corporations get - without corporate pricing and without corporate timelines.
We build, automate and grow. We work directly with the business owner, with no layers of account management, and we measure every project by what it changed in the business.
